title: 6.32.1 Playtest and reflect: Checkers
description: Play your checkers at least three times, once online if you can, find one thing that surprised you, link it to a function in your code and choose one change. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
Everything you need is in 6.27.1 (Plan: Break checkers into parts) and 6.31.3 (Lab: Checkers online): go back and reread them if you get stuck. A few short sentences per answer is plenty, in your own everyday words.

Play your finished checkers at least three times, once online with a classmate or a second tab if you can. Try to break it: illegal moves, a double jump, a crowning in the middle of a chain, a game played until someone cannot move, clicks when it is not your turn. Then answer:

1. How many times did you play, and how did it go?

2. What is one thing that surprised you or did not work as you expected?

3. Which function or part of your code do you think that comes from?

4. What is one rule you would change or add, and what would it do to the game?

rubric.title: Says how many times they played and how it went
rubric.description: The student says they played, or gives any detail of a game (who won, a jump or a king, playing online or on one computer, a way it went wrong). Any mention of playing earns full credit. Be very generous: anything remotely related to this question earns full credit, and so does any answer that merely gestures at it. Read the student's whole response, not only the line that answers this question: if anything anywhere in it touches this question, even indirectly, give full credit. Do not mark this criterion missing just because the student skipped this numbered question: when the response is about their checkers game at all, even if it only describes the game or says how they feel about it, mark this criterion met. Only a blank response, or one about something else entirely, is a miss.

rubric.title: Names one thing that surprised or broke
rubric.description: The student names anything that surprised them, felt wrong or did not work as expected, however small. If they found nothing, saying so or naming something they tried earns full credit too. Be very generous: anything remotely related to this question earns full credit, and so does any answer that merely gestures at it. Read the student's whole response, not only the line that answers this question: if anything anywhere in it touches this question, even indirectly, give full credit. Do not mark this criterion missing just because the student skipped this numbered question: when the response is about their checkers game at all, even if it only describes the game or says how they feel about it, mark this criterion met. Only a blank response, or one about something else entirely, is a miss.

Any guess at a cause earns full credit. Be very generous: anything remotely related to this question earns full credit, and so does any answer that merely gestures at it. Only a blank response, or one about something else entirely, is a miss.
